newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Ford Motor Credit and more.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Ford Motor Credit and more.

text.p: Asian debt markets started the week off big with a couple of hefty issues.
Ford Motor Credit launched a US$750 million Euro-Asian floating rate note issue through joint leads Lehman Brothers and Merrill Lynch.
The notes pay a margin of 12.5 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) and were priced at 99.847. Fees are 25 basis points.
The notes will be listed in Luxembourg, Hong Kong and Singapore.
This is the second time Ford Motor Credit has targetted an issue particularly to Asian investors. Its prior deal was a US$750 million fixed-rate Eurobond launched last May.

Lehman Brothers said in a release that the issue represents "a continuation of Ford Credit's strategic drive to provide different types of issues to meet investor demand in Europe and Asia and to increase its presence in the debt capital markets in the Asian region."
Other issuers also are eyeing Asian investors.
Bankers said lead managers JP Morgan and Merrill Lynch plan to roadshow Argentina's upcoming global bond in Hong Kong on Wednesday.
In Hong Kong, supranational Nordic Investment Bank launched a HK$1 billion seven-year bond.

The 7.37-percent bond was priced at 100.34 to yield 7.5103 percent, a spread of 39.5 basis points over the 6.80 percent Hong Kong Monetary Authority Exchange Fund Note due 2003 and 90 basis points over the interpolated U.S. Treasury note.
In other news from Hong Kong, New World PCS has mandated Deutsche Bank to arrange a HK$1.5 billion loan facility.
In New York on Friday, India's Reliance Industries set a two-tranche 144a bond via lead managers Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch.
The US$214 million 8.25 percent bond due in 2027 but puttable in 2007 was priced at par.
The US$100 million 10.25 percent century bond due 2097 was priced at 99.129 to yield 10.34 percent.
